en: The unscorched, the very red, the unharnessed, the black, the standing on the wings, the backbone, the inviolable, the unvanquished, the intermediate directions, the overseers, those who go to rest, the questions, the cows,
the similar ones, the teachers, those who have arrived, the full, the yoked, the egg-drinkers, the weapons, the narratives, the arrivals, the joys, those desiring, the bricks, the *ika*s.
These are impelled, emergent, watery,
and uniform in form.
The cultivated, those born from ploughed land, the fashioned, those fit for wells, desires, the base, those intent on forbearance,
the famous, those to be written down,
the hosts of Gandharvas, and the departed cowherds.
The drinkers of heat, the moon,
the people, the tongue born of the earth, and the nourishers of men.
The heated ones, those with copper chariots, those performing the *tapas*-born *stomas*,

the gods who are the guardians of the gods, the deities of the quarters, the radiant ordainers, the *darbha* grasses, the bestowers of wealth, the ancestral deities, those who uphold what was before, those who follow after the heroes,
the wise, the streams, and the sustainers.

The incalculable, the ancient, the newly defined, the bound, the unbound, the specific rules, the non-degrading, the ever-new, the secondary vital breaths, those that have entered, those that surround, the earthy, those directed westward, those nourished by water, the offspring, the protectors, the sacrificial cakes, the purifying, the milk-yielding, the protectors from afar, of the earth, those gone beyond, the scattering, the bestowing, the firmly established— those who know this are devoted to the Veda.
The Brahmins, those headed by the Brahmins;
the Bhāratas, wives, the earth,

brothers, rivals, honor, the hosts of Maruts, the great gods, mutual [relations], sacred hymns, honey-drinkers, the great compendiums, human beings, Muñja grass, moments, the wise, intoxications, and insights.
The worshipful ones desiring glory, those who have harnessed their own forms as sacrificers, the chariots, the reins, the gifts,
the dark-red worlds.
Vṛddhaśravas, Viśvavedas, Valgā, Vacanā, Varṇaviśeṣā, Vyavadātā, Vidyutā, Vaidyutā, Vyākhyātā, Vipatovataraśaviprā, Varcodā, Vidā, Varā,
Vāsāḥ, Vāḥ, Ahāparaḥ, Śeṣā, Śyāmāḥ, Śaṇḍilāḥ, Śravāḥ, Śaṃyudhāyā, Śvetāḥ, Śuddhasattvā, and Śritāḥ— there is none beyond her.

All armies, together with their followers, radiant as the sun, gathered, created, stationary, to be borne, self-existent, well-clothed, lunar, united, with rivals, heroic, extensive, winged, fixed, common, known together, and composed; the clouds, the waters, those placed beyond, those offered, darkness, snow, struck down, the invocations, the portions of the oblation, raw, swift, heroic, seated, northern, observers of the cosmic order, plants, knowing, divine, having seen, bestowing, not stealing, sinful, earths, to be cut apart, wintry, heavenly, existing, throbbing— may you harm them.

The body of Agni is the source of well-being; [it belongs] to Medhātithi, Aditi, Prajāpati, and Bṛhaspati. With horses not-yoked, with those who have arrived, with the subsequent Ukthāmadā gods, with winged ones, with unborn ones, with the Vāsava colors, with bodies, with thousands of hymns (stomas), with the two Aśvins, with the two intoxicated ones, with strength, with the two Jambhayas, with those two—the New and Full Moon sacrifices—on the two sides, on the two earths, on the out-breath and in-breath, on the two Pavamānas, on the two Bhavitas, on the two Deaths, on the two Vāyus, on the two Śamyus, in the hands: [all this is] Heaven.
The Aruṇaśamāna is complete.
Salutations to the glorious Hayagrīva, the Supreme Brahman.
